picks.title: Anthropic's Claude AI submitted false murder tip to Philadelphia police
picks.take: An AI chatbot reportedly filed a false murder tip with Philadelphia police. Clinicians know this pattern: a confident historian with no insight, fabricating collateral information. Nobody has yet proposed a capacity assessment for the software.

picks.title: GPT-6 and Intelligent UI for everyone
picks.take: GPT-6 arrives with an interface that generates visuals on demand. Medicine has long mastered the confident explanation delivered alongside a colorful diagram. Now the hallucinations get graphics, which will help in malpractice depositions.

picks.title: Disrupting AI-enabled “false front” operations
picks.take: OpenAI reports disrupting influence operations that used fake journalists and a fake think tank. Health misinformation has run this playbook for years, but it's reassuring to see the arsonist's equipment supplier doing the fire inspection.

picks.title: Sharing AI progress in mathematics
picks.take: OpenAI shares new results on open math problems, with formal Lean proofs posted for checking. Verifiable claims and public data: a standard clinical AI vendors could try, if the white paper and the pitch deck ever agreed on anything.

picks.title: Microsoft president says UK is best placed to drive AI regulation
picks.take: Microsoft's president says milk and washing machines get more oversight than AI companies. Fair, though in medicine we'd note that the milk never offered to summarize a patient chart and then confidently invented an allergy.

picks.title: Google rolls out improved SynthID AI content detector, now available globally
picks.take: Google's improved SynthID detector now flags AI content from several vendors, globally. Useful, though in medicine we've learned that a screening test is only as good as its sensitivity, specificity, and what anyone does after it comes back positive.

picks.title: Former Plaud exec raises $26M for AI app that listens to you in the background
picks.take: A startup raised $26M for an app that listens to you in the background so it can help better. Ambient scribes already taught clinicians this model: constant listening, then a note nobody asked for.

picks.title: Meta releases its first frontier model, Muse Wonder
picks.take: Meta releases Muse Wonder, its first frontier model, with higher benchmark scores. Benchmarks remain the AI industry's equivalent of surrogate endpoints: impressive, measurable, and only loosely related to whether the patient gets better.

picks.title: Microsoft’s new AI chip makes it less reliant on Nvidia’s GPUs
picks.take: Microsoft unveils its third-generation in-house Maia chip to reduce dependence on Nvidia. Every hospital understands vendor dependence, and that the best remedy is paying a different, much larger vendor to build your own.

picks.title: How Oracle turns days of work into minutes with ChatGPT and Codex
picks.take: Oracle reports turning days of work into minutes with ChatGPT and Codex. Healthcare administrators will recognize the promise: a saved week, reinvested immediately into additional documentation requirements for the same clinicians who were supposed to be saved.
